subject: Business
title: New-Market Disruption: Creating Demand That Didn't Exist
description: A short lesson to help you apply New-Market Disruption: Creating Demand That Didn't Exist.

hook.text: Nobody asked for a personal computer in 1975. Mainframe makers saw no demand. Apple and Microsoft saw an empty market.

buildup.text: New-market disruption creates customers who couldn't access the incumbent's product due to cost or complexity.

discovery.text: The transistor radio didn't compete with home stereos. It created a new market: teenagers listening to music anywhere.

twist.text: Surveys can't identify new markets. No one demands what they can't imagine. You have to build it and show them.

climax.text: Airbnb created a market of 'host your spare room' that hotels never imagined. Now it's worth more than Marriott.

punchline.text: The biggest markets are the ones that don't exist yet.

quiz.question: What defines a new-market disruption?
options: It creates customers who couldn't previously access the existing product
It improves the existing market leader's product
It raises prices to create exclusivity

details.summary: New market disruption creates products for customers who previously had no viable option, effectively growing the total market rather than stealing existing share. Sony's transistor radio, personal computers, and smartphones all created entirely new categories of consumers.
details.whyItMatters: New market disruption is less threatening to incumbents initially because it serves non-consumers rather than stealing their customers. By the time incumbents notice, the new market has grown large enough to encroach on their territory.
takeaways: New market disruption serves customers who had no previous solution
It grows total market size rather than redistributing existing demand
Incumbents often ignore it because it does not initially affect their customers

faq.question: How does new market disruption differ from low-end disruption?
faq.answer: Low-end disruption targets overserved existing customers with simpler, cheaper offerings. New market disruption targets non-consumers who previously could not access or afford any solution. Sony's transistor radio did not steal from RCA; it brought music to teenagers who had none.

faq.question: How do you identify opportunities for new market disruption?
faq.answer: Look for tasks that people want to accomplish but cannot because existing solutions are too expensive, complex, or inaccessible. Ask what barriers prevent non-consumers from participating. When technology reduces those barriers by an order of magnitude, new market disruption becomes possible.
